utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have just one more question to ask you about this. Do you know how were documents safeguarded in your battalion? How were they kept?

utterances.speaker: MITAR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing special. I believe that all the paper work was taken to the brigade. I don't know who the paper work was handed over because I was not involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it done periodically, for example, after a month or so?

utterances.speaker: MITAR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. I know that I would be returning payrolls to the brigade. When all the people signed the payroll, I would return it to the brigade. That's what I know because I was in charge of that. For the rest, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who it was who decided when documents would be taken to the brigade? Was it you?

utterances.speaker: MITAR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It wasn't me. I don't know exactly who it was. I suppose it was all under the commander's authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This would be all. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. We've got ten minutes before the break. Either Mr. Sarapa or Mr. Ostojic, whoever wishes to go first.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, we'll have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Then it has to be you, Mr. Sarapa, and if you could finish in ten minutes, it's better than getting the witness back after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please have a minute or so to consult with my client before I start cross-examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Sarapa. And if you need to leave the courtroom with him, consult him outside, we'll make sure that that is possible. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That would be much appreciated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have questions for the witness. Do you wish to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [In English] Yes, I have just a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which will take you how long?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we will finish before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me introduce myself, sir, I represent General Pandurevic. I will only have a few questions for you, very short questions. Can the witness please be shown the document we have just seen, which is P295? Page 354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the document is under seal so we need to go into private session or not broadcast, anyway, depending on the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if we could go to private session for my questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now, thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: You've already told us that private lorries were also engaged and you mentioned a name of the person from Rocevic who owned these lorries and they were used to take people to the front line. Was that an agreement between the command and that person himself?

utterances.speaker: MITAR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether Djoko Nikolic and Dragan Jovic who were the owners of these lorries and who did that? Who were engaged in that transport?

utterances.speaker: MITAR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Djoko Nikolic was all the time and Dragan Jovic on occasion, he used somebody else's lorry. But I don't know whose lorry he used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you. But that was a civilian lorry, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MITAR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: I thank you. I have no further questions for you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Sarapa. Mr. Vanderpuye, do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I don't, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Vanderpuye. We don't have any further questions for you, Mr. Lazarevic, which means you are free to go. Your testimony has finished, has ended. On behalf of the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for having come over to give testimony, and on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a 25-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the position? The next witness is Witness number 105. Are you in a position to start with him today or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what I wanted to make sure of. So you start with him tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime can we do anything in these --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, there is one issue that I would -- I'd like to bring up to the Court. I've been discussing it with my colleagues from the Borovcanin team. Well, for many months now, we have been in discussions with them letting them know that we planned to bring eventually Alastair Graham to testify and to play the taped interview of the Accused Borovcanin. They have indicated to us that they had believed they were going to challenge the admissibility of that interview, and I know that they are very busy and they haven't done that yet. Now, for the eight days that we have leading up to the break, this interview would be, and Alastair Graham would be a good witness because it doesn't affect General Tolimir so much, and so we have -- well, several days ago -- listed Alastair Graham as the -- as a witness for July, and I've been in discussions with my colleagues and I know they are -- well, I'm not exactly sure what they are planning on doing now but we -- the sooner we know, I've always told them the sooner we know the better we are for planning, and because if they do file a written challenge, that may hold up our ability to put them in July. If they don't, then perhaps we can talk about the logistics of 15 hours of interview, whether or not we play the whole thing, which is usually the simplest but that will be -- I don't know how the Court feels about that either but that's normally, when we have an accused, we play the whole thing. But I may be able to reach something with the Defence that we play parts of it that they want and parts that we -- and of course you would get the whole thing but those are the discussion that we are having, but we are getting so close to that time period that I wanted to bring that to your attention because if those 15 hours are not something we can use, we are going to really be scrambling for witnesses. But that's where we are, and I just wanted to alert you to that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you wish to comment now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, very briefly. I mean we are in contact with the Prosecution. We are discussing this issue for some period. It is not just the question whether Mr. Graham will come at the beginning of July or not. There are quite a few issue that we already were trying to resolve and there is still -- well, I have to say, there is no answer from the Prosecution side. We are discussing first the possibility -- we are definitely confirming that we will oppose the admissibility of this interview. It was our intention to come into an agreement with the Prosecution about the transcript of this interview. Our case manager is making great effort in order to review these interview, to review the transcript, and we sent to the Prosecution our version of the transcript of this interview and asked them for their reply. So far, we still haven't received that yet. It was my intention to discuss this again with the Prosecution. This could save a lot of court time if we agree upon the transcript of the interview. Maybe it won't be necessary, once it is decided in the case, that the Trial Chamber decides to listen to it. Most of our objections to the interview have to be reviewed by the Trial Chamber by looking at the transcript itself. So we are trying now to discuss this with the Prosecution and we will supply the Trial Chamber with the transcript, which is agreed between the two sides, and we will draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to some parts of this transcript for which we believe that will be of interest in reaching a decision on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do have their transcript and we are working on it, and we have disclosed a revised transcript ourselves on 3 May and I don't really think we will have a problem coming to an agreement on a transcript. That's not the kind of issue we would normally have a problem with so that I don't see as a problem. And I don't know if there is anything else they are requesting and I frankly don't understand what they mean when they say there are portions that they are going to be challenging, and whether that is -- has something to do with translation or something about the way the question was asked or something else. That's the first I've heard of that. But as you can see, this could get complicated and they have not filed anything yet, so I'm just for planning purposes, I welcome whatever they have in mind, but this is really making planning difficult and we put it off until this time, but I don't think we can put it off any longer and it's my intention to call this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think we have two elements that are important. One is what Mr. Lazarevic has mentioned, that if we have a formal application from you to bring forward this witness and a formal objection to that request by the Borovcanin team, then the question of a transcript comes into play, especially since it's being submitted that we need to look at the transcript before we are able to decide. I would imagine that that is partly true but that the motion itself can be decided also on other issues. That being so, I think now the Borovcanin team have been put on notice formally that it is the intention of the Prosecution to bring this witness forward to give evidence at the earliest possible, so I think it's the time for the Borovcanin team to articulate its objection, and for the two of you to sit down and see if you can provide us with a transcript which -- on which you agree, and if you don't -- if there are parts of that transcript that you still don't agree upon, you identify them to us so that we'll be in a position to know how best to proceed with this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That will be no problem. And I may suggest that -- the witness is actually 97 I'm told that's next in line, and that witness may not take all of tomorrow and certainly I think we could have Friday to actually orally argue this motion and to get out the guts of this on Friday and if the Court wanted written submissions after that, or if the Borovcanin team felt they needed written submissions, that would be fine. But we could really move this ball forward if we could do this orally on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Because I was getting a little bit confused because you said Witness 97 and in the records I have it shows as number 105 but then it shows also as Witness 97, you are correct, yes. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, if I can very briefly reply, it is not just the issue much the transcripts. Okay, I will definitely be in touch with Mr. McCloskey and we will resolve this issue somehow. It was our understanding based on one of the submissions, I cannot say I was kind of taken aback this moment by raising this issue at this point, but basically one of the submissions, it was said by the Prosecution that they intend to put the interview of Mr. Borovcanin to their 65 ter list. So it was our understanding that the ball is on Prosecution side, that they are to initiate this by asking a formal by placing a formal motion to the Trial Chamber to add Mr. Borovcanin's interview on the Rule 65 ter list of the Prosecution. And then we will be able to give our reply and object at this point. So that was our understanding. At this point I would like some guide lines from the Trial Chamber whether this is the situation or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't tell you that, but what is of concern to me and I speak for myself, is that we are already at the 11th hour, and I suggest that if you need to move on -- move this, that you do so as quickly in a formal manner, because I don't expect the Borovcanin team to take a position unless they know exactly what your intentions are, I mean, and you've made them clear now, but I think you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll expect further from you. One needs to -- yes, Mr. McCloskey? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I just would like to clarify something. It's just the position of the Prosecution that we have made our intentions regarding Alistair Graham and the interview with Mr. Borovcanin crystal clear from 28 April 2006, where when we provided our 65 ter list we stated that Graham will introduce and testify about the statements taken from accused Borovcanin. This has been crystal clear to the Defence for as long as this has been in their possession, and we have been -- because we get along very well with the Defence, when are your challenge coming, when, when, when? And they have, you know, as I say, they have witness busy, they haven't done anything. So this is not me now coming clear with this. This was clear many months ago and we have eight days that we need to fill up and the time is here for that, and if they would like to argue this on Friday, we are here to argue it. These kinds of motions are argued every day in courts throughout the world. We don't need long filings and long periods of responses. This is something that we can get started on now and filings can follow, and you can give us your direction on this. I would like to, if we can, get going on it because that will take some of the pressure of trying to find witnesses to fill those other dates as well as it's time to move.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. When I mentioned in some of Prosecution submissions it was stated that it will be a formal request to amend Rule 65 ter list, now I can maybe be more specific. It is scheduling order for witnesses for the month of July 2007 which we received and here it says that "interview of Ljubomir Borovcanin 20 February 2002 and 11 March 2002 will be subject of motion to amend 65 ter exhibit list." So this was the starting point for our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not get bogged down by technicalities. We are fixing Friday as a date to have this debated, where the formal request will be made and discussed, particularly by you, Mr. Lazarevic, and of course the Prosecution. We've got only a couple of minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've got a couple of minutes left. There are two pending motions of which the Trial Chamber is now going to issue oral decisions. These are basically moot motions, but for the record we have to declare them so. Firstly on 11 June counsel for accused Beara and Nikolic filed the joint defence motion seeking leave to reply and reply to Prosecution response to joint defence request on behalf of Beara, Ljubisa Beara, and Drago Nikolic for certification of the Trial Chamber's decision on defence motion seeking reconsideration of two Trial Chamber decisions related to Witness 108. Earlier on the same day, the Trial Chamber had issued its decision on joint Beara and Nikolic request for certification to appeal the Trial Chamber's decision denying reconsideration of two decisions related to Witness PW 108, with a consequence that the motion seeking leave to reply is therefore moot, and it is being declared so. Secondly, on the 22nd of June, the Prosecution filed a motion for leave to amend the 65 ter list with five expert reports related to Witness Dr. Barr. It sought leave for 65 ter list of experts to be supplemented with five expert reports written by and relevant to her testimony. She testified on Monday and Tuesday of this week. The five expert reports which were subject of the motion were admitted at the end of her testimony. In the circumstances, this motion, too, is now moot and being declared so. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Yes, Mr. Bourgon, be quick. We've only got one minute left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Is there anything coming from the Registry concerning the consequences of the possibility of a joinder and if not, we will be in touch with the Trial Chamber's legal officer because the Prosecution's case needs to be extended passed 15 August in order for the legal aid regime to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that we can take care of --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- and I think we can coordinate, and I don't know if there is a letter from the registrar to you in the offing. I haven't got it. But I'll try to find out. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you. One moment, because Mr. Vanderpuye doesn't agree with the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, I just we don't have any documents to tender in relation to the testimony of the witness that had previously been discharged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can deal with it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of June, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
